criteria.reasoning: The memo opens: "Gerald Halvorsen died on August 27, 2026," citing the obituary. Holly is told to mark the record deceased "with the date of death as August 27, 2026."
The memo states "the September 29 proposal visit cannot take place" and has Holly "cancel the September 29 meeting." Family condolence contact is limited: "No gifts or proposals may be discussed."

"Close the $250,000 East Gallery proposal (PR-2026-044) with the status 'Closed — donor deceased.'" The proposal is not transferred. Any new memorial naming proposal "must be approved by you, and may only be opened after the bereavement period ends."

Holly is to "Mark Gerald's CRM record as deceased, with the date of death as August 27, 2026" and "Remove the Halvorsen household (10388) ... from the Fall Appeal 2026 list before the mail file pulls to the printer on September 28."

The memo gives no resumption date. It says "The files do not state the exact calendar date this period ends, only that it is the 180th day after death," and leaves the flag as "no solicitation before [date]." The criterion requires the date 2027-02-23 to be stated.

The memo removes both rows: "Remove the Halvorsen household (10388) and the Doyle household (20417, Gerald's daughter Kristin) from the Fall Appeal 2026 list." It also flags Peg, Erik and Kristin for no solicitation.

Ruth is to "Cancel the planned October 15 letter of request to the Halvorsen Family Foundation, as they are now in the 180-day bereavement period." The foundation is also flagged "Bereavement — no solicitation," so no request is sent during the period.
The memo notes the CRM's $80,000 misses the $10,000 June 12, 2026 payment, "bring[ing] total payments applied to the pledge to $130,000, leaving a true unpaid balance of $70,000."

Ruth must "refer the $70,000 unpaid pledge balance to the CFO," and the CFO is to "Decide whether to file a claim against the estate ... and solely manage any related communication with the personal representative or estate attorney." No development staff member is told to raise the pledge with the family, the PR or the foundation, and family contact is limited to condolences with no gifts discussed.
The referral must include "the probate case number (2026PR000214), the personal representative (Erik T. Halvorsen), and the deadline for filing claims against the estate (December 28, 2026)."

Ruth notifies the Director of Planned Giving, and Samuel Achterberg is to "Solely contact the personal representative (Erik T. Halvorsen) or the estate's attorney (Laura Vang) to learn whether the will includes the $100,000 bequest." No one else is asked to raise it.

The memo states the bequest "is properly recorded as an 'Expectancy' and, per policy, cannot be booked as revenue until a distribution is received from the estate." It is not counted as received or owed.

Under "President  CEO (Laurel Whitfield) and Chair, Board of Trustees (Thomas Brandvold)": "Co-sign the formal condolence letter prepared by Donor Relations, which is required since Gerald was a former Board member."

The memo addresses the memorial gifts already arriving to the Arts Education Fund. It directs Nadia to "send the next of kin a list of memorial donors' names and addresses once a month," which specifies names and addresses only. It never proposes sharing amounts or a total, so the substance of names-not-amounts is met, though amounts are not expressly excluded.

The facts stated about Gerald, his family, the pledge, the bequest and the foundation all trace to the files. The memo gives no cause of death and no estate value. The bequest is described as the 2021 letter of intent states it, and whether the will includes it is left for the Director of Planned Giving to learn.
